title: Birth in Tremé and the dance halls there
summary: Justin gives his birth date and describes the Tremé halls (Cooperators, Economy, San Jacinto) and the 'banquet' dances.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: My name is George Justin, and I was born in New Orleans on the 17th day of September, 1915.
What part of town were you born in?

That was considered more or less the Tremes section of New Orleans, where there was always quite a bit of activity with the location of the Cooperators Hall, the Economy Hall, and later the San Jacinto Club, which were all wonderful places for jazz, wherein there was always something going on at various times during the week, if it wasn't a dance, as we used to call it a banquet. How do you spell it? That's the term. They used to say banquet, but that's the Creole pronunciation of it, I guess, was banquet.
You know, old Mercinians said they called sorays or something.
Oh yes. Uh-huh. And every time you heard that expression, you always knew just where to go, whether it was the Economy Hall or the Cooperators Hall or the San Jacinto Club.
The Cooperators Hall, is that what they used to call the old Hoax Hall too? It's a church there on Tremes?
It's a church right on Tremes, which was formerly called Liberty Street.
Yeah, I went to church there once.
